banka-mt-1.title: Fundamentals
q: What happens in the economy and in banking when the central bank raises interest rates?
Cost of credit: loan, credit, interest, expensive
Demand / inflation: demand, inflation, consumption
Deposits: deposit, saving
Exchange rate effect: exchange rate, currency, capital inflow
Bank profitability: margin, net interest, profitab

When the policy rate rises, borrowing costs go up and loan demand falls; this aims to slow consumption and bring inflation down. Higher deposit rates make saving more attractive. Foreign capital inflows can ease pressure on the currency. For banks, the net interest margin changes depending on how quickly deposit and loan pricing adjusts.
What are the main items on a bank's balance sheet?
Loans: loan
Deposits: deposit
Equity: equity, capital
Securities / liquidity: securit, liquidity, cash
Capital adequacy: capital adequacy, risk

On the asset side the largest item is loans, along with securities and liquid assets. On the liability side the largest source is deposits, plus other funding and equity. The ratio of equity to risk-weighted assets shows capital adequacy.

banka-mt-2.title: Case & Group Exercise
q: A branch lends less than its competitors in the region. How would you analyze why?
Comparing data: data, compar, market share
Customer segment: segment, sme, retail
Process / approval time: approval time, process, speed
Pricing: interest, pric
Action plan: action, campaign, visit

First I compare the branch's loan volume, customer count and market share with the region and competitors. I break it down by product and customer segment to see where the gap is. I separate causes such as approval times and pricing. Based on the findings I propose an action plan with targeted customer visits and process improvements.

banka-kredi-1.title: Credit Assessment
q: What do you look at when lending to a company?
Financial statements: balance sheet, income statement, cash flow
Repayment capacity: repay, cash, debt service
Leverage / ratios: debt, ratio, leverage, liquidity
Collateral: collateral, mortgage, guarantee
Sector / management: sector, industry, management, background

First I use the financial statements to examine the company's profitability, debt and liquidity. The key question is whether its cash flow can repay the loan. I assess sector risk, the track record of the owners and management, and credit intelligence. Collateral is a secondary safeguard and shouldn't be the basis of the lending decision.

banka-kredi-2.title: Risk Case
q: A company you lent to has started paying late. What do you do?
Early warning: early warning, late, monitor
Meeting the customer: meet, why, visit
Restructuring: restructur, term, plan
Collateral / legal action: collateral, legal, enforce

I take the early warning signal seriously and meet the company right away to understand whether the delay is temporary or lasting. I review the latest financials and cash flow. If the problem is temporary I propose a suitable restructuring plan. If it's lasting I review the collateral and, if needed, start legal proceedings.

banka-musteri-1.title: Branch Fundamentals
q: How would you offer a new credit card to a customer who comes into the branch?
Understanding the need: need, question, habit
Suitable product: suit, advantage, campaign
Transparency: fee, interest, transparen
Consent / no pressure: without pressure, pressure

First I ask questions to understand the customer's spending habits and needs. I highlight the benefits that suit them, such as instalments or points campaigns. I explain costs such as the annual fee and interest transparently. I leave the decision to the customer and don't pressure them.

banka-musteri-2.title: Difficult Situations
q: An angry customer says there were unauthorized transactions on their card. What do you do?
Calm reception: calm, empath, listen
Blocking the card: block, cancel, freeze
Dispute process: dispute, chargeback, record
Keeping them informed: time, inform, follow up

I listen calmly and show that I understand their concern. First I block the card immediately to stop any new transactions. I open a dispute for the suspicious transactions and clearly explain how long the process will take and what happens next. I keep the customer informed throughout.

kabin-1.title: Fundamentals
q: Why do you want to become a flight attendant?
Guest focus: guest, passenger, service
Safety awareness: safety, security
Personal fit: people, communicat, team, flexib
Concrete example: for example, experience

I enjoy communicating with people and giving them a good experience; for example, I won a customer satisfaction award in my previous job. I know the role isn't only about service but first of all about being responsible for passengers' safety. I adapt well to irregular hours and teamwork.
During a flight a passenger refuses to fasten their seat belt. What do you do?
Polite reminder: polite, kind, explain
Reason: safety, rule, turbulence
Step-by-step escalation: again, senior, captain
Other passengers: other passenger, calm

First I politely explain to the passenger why the seat belt is mandatory and that it's for their safety. If they insist, I keep a calm tone and remind them of the rule again. If they still refuse, I report it to the senior cabin crew member, and the captain is informed if needed. Meanwhile I make sure not to disturb the other passengers.

kabin-2.title: Crisis Situations
q: A passenger becomes ill during the flight. What do you do?
Assessing the situation: assess, conscious, breath
Informing the crew and captain: crew, captain, inform
Calling for medical staff: doctor, medical, announce
First aid: first aid, oxygen, kit
Documentation: record, report

First I assess the passenger's consciousness and breathing and start first aid in line with my training. I inform my crew and the captain immediately. If needed, an announcement asks whether there is a doctor or medical professional on board, and oxygen and first aid kits are used. I report the incident according to procedure.

pilot-1.title: Fundamentals
q: What is CRM (Crew Resource Management) and why is it important?
Definition: crew resource management, crm
Communication: communicat, open, speak up
Decision making: decision, situational awareness
Human error: human error, accident

CRM is an approach that helps the crew use all available resources effectively in the cockpit and cabin. It covers open communication, sharing the workload, situational awareness and joint decision making. Because human error plays a part in most accidents, CRM is one of the cornerstones of flight safety.

pilot-2.title: Decision Making
q: You think the captain is making a wrong decision. What do you do?
Speaking up: say, speak up, voice, raise my concern
Respectful but clear: respect, clear
Relying on information: data, indicator, instrument, procedure
Escalating: again, insist, safety

I raise my concern respectfully but clearly, based on the indicators I see and the procedure. If the captain doesn't respond, I repeat it more directly. If safety is directly at risk I insist, following CRM principles; hierarchy must never come before safety.

otel-1.title: Guest Relations
q: How do you handle a guest who has a reservation but there's no room available?
Apology and ownership: apolog, responsib, ownership
Quick solution: alternative, upgrade, another hotel
Compensation: compensat, complimentary, discount
Follow-up: follow up, manager

First I sincerely apologize and take ownership of the problem. I offer an alternative right away: a higher category room or, if that's not possible, a nearby partner hotel with transport. I offer compensation for the inconvenience, such as a complimentary service or a discount. I follow up with the guest together with the manager so they leave satisfied.

otel-2.title: Operations
q: The cleanliness score in guest reviews is falling. What do you do?
Data analysis: review, score, analy
Root cause: root cause, staff, time, inspect
Working with the department: housekeeping, team
Monitoring: checklist, track, measure

First I analyze the reviews to see which rooms and issues the complaints concentrate on. With the housekeeping team I discuss root causes, such as staffing levels or time per room. I introduce a checklist and random inspections and track the scores weekly.

banka-mt-3.title: Strategy
q: As a bank moves to digital channels, what role should its branch network play?
Customer segments: segment
Digital transactions: digital, mobile
Advice centre: advi, complex
Cost and efficiency: cost, efficien
Staff transformation: staff, skill

As simple transactions move to mobile and digital channels, the branch’s role has to change. I would split customers into segments and look at which groups really need a branch. Branches should become advice centres for complex needs such as loans, investments and SME finance. The number and format of branches should be replanned using cost and efficiency data. This shift needs training that builds staff skills in advising customers.

banka-kredi-3.title: Portfolio Risk
q: You spot concentration risk in one sector in the loan portfolio. What do you recommend?
Concentration analysis: concentrat, share
Stress test: stress test, scenario
Limit policy: limit
Pricing and collateral: pric, collateral
Report to committee: committee, report

First I measure the sector’s share of the portfolio and the concentration in the largest borrowers. I run a stress test with a scenario such as falling demand in the sector and estimate the possible loss. I propose a limit for the sector and steer new lending to other sectors. I price loans in the risky sector more tightly and strengthen collateral terms. I present the findings and an action plan to the credit committee in a report.

banka-musteri-3.title: Branch Leadership
q: How do you raise your customer representatives’ sales without hurting customer satisfaction?
Balanced targets: satisfaction, balance
Needs-based selling: need
Coaching: coaching, observ, feedback
Measurement: nps, complaint
Recognition: recogni

At my previous branch, complaints rose when targets went up; my goal was to balance sales and satisfaction. With the team I built a sales conversation flow focused on the customer’s needs, not the product. I observed each rep’s meetings and gave one-on-one coaching and feedback. I added NPS and the number of complaints to the scorecard next to sales. As a result sales increased by 15% and complaints fell; I recognised the successes in team meetings.

kabin-3.title: Cabin Leadership
q: As a cabin manager, two crew members on your team are in conflict during a flight. What do you do?
Safety first: safety
Separate, calm talk: separate, calm
Reassign duties: duties, dut
Resolve after the flight: after the flight, debrief
Report: report

On one flight I noticed two colleagues arguing during the service. My first priority was that safety and the guest experience were not affected. I had a short, calm talk with each of them separately in the galley. To ease the tension I changed the duties for the rest of the flight. In the debrief after the flight we talked it through together and resolved it, and I wrote a short report as required.

pilot-3.title: Captaincy & CRM
q: As captain, you notice your first officer hesitates to point out your mistakes. What do you do?
Open communication: open, encourag
Briefing: briefing
CRM principles: crm
Feedback: feedback
Lead by example: admitted my mistake, admit

On one flight I saw that my first officer noticed a deviation of mine but mentioned it late. In the briefing on the next flights I clearly asked them to speak up about anything and encouraged them to do so. Under CRM principles, hierarchy in the cockpit must never come before safety. After the flight I gave honest feedback and asked for feedback in return. I admitted my mistake to set an example, and our communication on later flights was much more open.

otel-3.title: Hotel Management
q: The hotel’s guest review score has been dropping for months. What action plan do you make?
Review analysis: review, theme
Root cause: department, root cause
Staff training: staff, training
Quick wins: quick
Reply and track: repl, track

First I read the recent reviews and pull out recurring themes. I split complaints by department and find the root cause in areas such as housekeeping, breakfast or check-in. I act quickly on problems that can be fixed fast and plan staff training in the departments with issues. I reply to negative reviews personally and with a solution. I track the score weekly and share the results with the team.
